acceptance_test_matrix: Config semantic coverage: every existing /api/config/* endpoint is exercised with domain=equities and domain=crypto, asserting runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, and venue list are domain-correct.

Diagnostics semantic coverage: every existing /api/diagnostics/* endpoint is exercised with domain=equities and domain=crypto, asserting crypto payloads do not leak equities identifiers and equities payloads remain unchanged.
Equities regression coverage: omitted domain and explicit domain=equities preserve existing response shapes, status codes, identifiers, and venue lists.
Crypto edge-case coverage: unsupported domain and missing crypto hot-view/config data follow existing resolution or availability behavior without equities fallback leakage.
Request isolation coverage: alternating equities and crypto requests do not cross-contaminate cached or request-scoped runtime metadata.
Playwright coverage: UI domain selector switches between equities and crypto and validates domain-scoped config or diagnostics data through the browser-facing route layer.
Configured QA gate coverage: ./gradlew :app-api:test, UI Playwright e2e, ./qa/smoke.sh, and ./qa/regression.sh complete successfully before final PR handoff.
assumptions: The domain query parameter supports at least equities and crypto, with omitted domain preserving the existing default equities behavior.
Existing app-api config and diagnostics controllers own request parameter resolution and response assembly for UI-facing endpoints.
Crypto runtime metadata already exists in Redis hot views, existing config providers, or existing runtime metadata projections and must be selected rather than created through mutation paths.
The UI domain selector already exists or can be covered through narrow test-only selector stabilization without changing product behavior.
Missing crypto data must surface through existing unavailability or diagnostics semantics rather than falling back to equities data.

critic.rationale: The plan is generally well-structured and includes the required QA, review, lifecycle, persistence, concurrency, and human-gated merge controls. The main blocking issue is global forbidden-path overlap: several slices forbid paths that other slices explicitly allow, especially source-vs-test ownership boundaries. A secondary compactness concern exists because the roadmap item is fairly narrow but uses five slices plus design/review/QA gates.

acceptance_tests: Every existing /api/config/* endpoint is exercised with domain=equities and domain=crypto, asserting domain-correct runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, and venue list.
Every existing /api/diagnostics/* endpoint is exercised with domain=equities and domain=crypto, asserting domain-correct runtime metadata and no new endpoint paths.
Default-domain and explicit domain=equities calls preserve existing identifiers, response shapes, status codes, and venue lists.
Crypto responses do not expose equities graphId, runtimeConfigVersion, venue list, live config, partition state identifiers, or diagnostics identifiers.
Alternating equities and crypto requests do not cross-contaminate request-scoped or cached runtime metadata.
Unsupported or missing domain follows existing resolution behavior without introducing new mutation or repair semantics.
Missing crypto hot-view or config data produces existing availability semantics without falling back to equities identifiers.
Playwright selector-switch coverage exercises equities and crypto and verifies domain-scoped config or diagnostics behavior through the browser-facing route layer.
./gradlew :app-api:test, the UI Playwright command, ./qa/smoke.sh, and ./qa/regression.sh pass before final PR handoff.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Domain selection must remain request scoped and be passed explicitly through controller and service calls. Do not introduce static mutable selected-domain state, thread-local selected-domain state, request-order-dependent caching, or shared controller state that can leak one request domain into another.
forbidden_alternatives: Using UI-only filtering while app-api still returns equities payloads for crypto requests.
Hard-coding crypto identifiers in tests without validating endpoint payloads.
Changing runtime graph production code to compensate for an API selection bug.
Introducing global mutable domain state or cache entries not keyed by domain.
Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, Drizzle, or another app-api persistence layer.
hard_constraints: Do not add new /api/diagnostics/crypto or other domain-specific endpoint trees.
Do not add POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE config mutation APIs.
Do not introduce persistence or repair behavior for selected domain.
Do not patch or vendor dag-framework locally.
Do not modify platform-runtime, ingest, historical-store, opportunities, signals, or cockpit behavior for this parity pass.
Keep implementation compact and focused on config and diagnostics parity plus selector-switch coverage.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: app-api controllers and read-model services own request-scoped domain selection and response assembly. QA owns tests and fixtures only. UI work is limited to Playwright selector-switch coverage and narrow selector stabilization if needed. platform-runtime, ingest adapters, historical stores, dag-framework, and mutation endpoint ownership are not expanded.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: This feature is read-only. app-api may read existing Redis hot views, existing config providers, and existing metadata projections, but must not write Redis, QuestDB, files, historical stores, config state, or any OLTP store as part of config or diagnostics endpoint handling.
design_contract.public_api: Existing GET /api/config/* and GET /api/diagnostics/* endpoints accept optional ?domain=equities|crypto and keep their current response shapes. Crypto requests resolve runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, diagnostics metadata, and venue lists from crypto-scoped read models. Equities requests, including omitted-domain calls, preserve existing identifiers, status codes, payload shapes, and venue lists.

final.problem_statement: Implement read-only crypto-domain parity for existing GET /api/config/* and GET /api/diagnostics/* endpoints so ?domain=crypto returns crypto-scoped runtime metadata, config, diagnostics, partition state, and venues while explicit or default equities behavior remains unchanged.
risk_register: Endpoint inventory may miss a config or diagnostics handler unless the design slice enumerates every mapped route before QA authoring.
Domain parsing may be threaded through only some controller/service branches, causing partial crypto parity or silent equities fallback.
Shared runtime metadata caching may leak the previous request domain unless data is request scoped or cache keys include domain.
Venue lists are prone to mixed-domain leakage because equities and crypto identifiers may live behind shared config helpers.
Crypto metadata may be absent from current hot-view fixtures, requiring tests that distinguish existing unavailable-data semantics from equities fallback leakage.
Playwright selector coverage can pass visually while API responses remain wrong unless network assertions or domain-scoped UI data assertions are included.
Regression risk is concentrated in preserving equities defaults and avoiding new read/write boundaries in app-api.
